Who funded autism research in 2019 and 2020?
14 federal agencies
16 private organizations
30 funders 
provided funding data 
for this report.
The 2019-2020 IACC Autism Research Portfolio Analysis Report provides comprehensive information about 
the status of autism research funding among federal agencies and private research organizations 
in the United States, featuring analysis of funding trends in autism research from 2008-2020. This 
At-a-Glance version provides a summary of key findings included in the report. The full report can be 
found here: https://iacc.hhs.gov/publications/portfolio-analysis/2020/ 
Thank you to all funders who contributed to this report!
AT-A-GLANCE
2
INTERAGENCY AUTISM COORDINATING COMMITTEE
How much autism research was funded from 2008 to 2020?
• U.S. autism research was funded at the 
highest ever levels in 2019 and 2020.
• Federal agencies accounted for 
approximately 82% of total funding.
• Private organizations accounted for almost 
18% of total funding. 
• Factors possibly contributing to funding 
fluctuations include:
 – New or ending initiatives
 – Changes in organization budgets and 
priorities
 – Changes in government appropriations
 – Differences in funding mechanisms
 – Potential impacts of COVID-19 pandemic

4
INTERAGENCY AUTISM COORDINATING COMMITTEE
Which areas of autism research were funded in 2019 and 2020?
Autism research funding in 2019 and 2020 supported projects relevant to all seven Questions of the 
2016-2017 IACC Strategic Plan.
Screening & 
Diagnosis
How can I recognize the signs of autism, and why is early detection so important?
Examples of research topics: diagnostic and screening tools, early signs and biomarkers, reduce disparities in early 
diagnosis, spectrum of characteristics
Biology
What is the biology underlying autism?
Examples of research topics: brain structure and function, cognitive studies, language development and communication, 
co-occurring conditions, molecular pathways, sensory and motor function, sex and gender differences
Genetic & 
Environmental 
Factors
What causes autism, and can the disabling aspects of autism be prevented or preempted?
Examples of research topics: gene-environment interactions, genetic factors, environmental factors
Interventions
What treatments and interventions will help?
Examples of research topics: communication/augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), behavioral, 
educational, pharmacological/medicinal, dietary, occupational, and technology-based interventions
Services & 
Supports
What kinds of services and supports are needed to maximize quality of life for people on the autism spectrum?
Examples of research topics: community inclusion, education, service delivery, practitioner training, safety , reduce 
disparities in service access and outcomes
Lifespan
How can we meet the needs of people on the autism spectrum as they progress into and through adulthood?
Examples of research topics: employment, housing, daily life skills, health outcomes, health care systems, transition to 
adulthood, postsecondary outcomes, aging
Infrastructure 
& Prevalence
How do we continue to build, expand, and enhance the infrastructure system to meet the needs of the 
autism community? 
Examples of research topics: data tools, prevalence, research infrastructure, research workforce
